picks.reasoning: Stubborn call: I back the stronger players, and BLG has them. Viper on the bot lane is a series-winning individual, and the LPL-LEC gap is real, so I'm not going to get cute and trust MKOI's scrappy comeback story. MKOI will make it ugly and throw some chaos at BLG, but class wins out, and BLG already beat them once this summer.

Tempo, tempo, tempo! BLG wins the first 15 minutes more often, with Jarvan or Naafiri pathing to first objectives and Viper's bot lane turning that early lead into a snowball, and they've already beaten MKOI once this event. MKOI's Lee Sin can crack a game open early, but they lean on comebacks and have a habit of throwing leads. I don't trust that against an LPL side that closes out its leads, and the region gap tilts it further to BLG.

This one comes down to the draft, and BLG's pool is just deeper: Yunara and Lulu in the bot lane are comfortable, flexible picks, and Viper is the kind of star who punishes any slip. MKOI love their Ryze and Lee Sin comfort, but under Fearless those get picked apart fast. The LPL-versus-LEC gap is real, and BLG already beat them once this summer, so I'm backing BLG to out-draft and out-execute them.

This is where the numbers get loud: BLG have a 50-12 series record and already beat MKOI 1-0 at EWC this summer. MKOI's 0-2 record against other regions tells me they haven't passed that test yet. BLG's Viper at 31% damage share is the engine, and a best of 1 gives MKOI's comeback habit very little room to work. I won't go higher than the low 70s, because BLG have thrown leads before.

BLG walk in with the calm of a team that has been through finals and trusts each other when the pressure's on, and Viper and that Lulu pairing is pure chemistry. MKOI have heart and some real spark, but they've been shaky closing out games and have never been on a stage like this, so I'm backing the veterans' mood to hold the room.
